item.title: Advanced EtherCAT and Commissioning
item.description: Scope This page covers the lower-level EtherCAT and commissioning helpers that are available when the normal addSlave.cmd and applyComponent.cmd path is not enough. Use it when you need: additional EtherCAT domains custom process-image pointers/data items cyclic copying between EtherCAT entries runtime read/write access to individual SDOs explicit distributed-clock setup slave identity verification firmware update over FoE topology gaps where one or more slave positions should be skipped longer EtherCAT OP-state startup timeout during commissioning For the common Max wait time 30 second(s) startup message, see EtherCAT startup timeout before changing lower-level EtherCAT settings.

item.title: ESI Parser
item.description: Scope This page documents the legacy EtherCAT ESI parser utility. The tool parses an EtherCAT ESI XML file, filters slaves by name and revision, optionally filters alternative PDO mappings, and can export: a JSON summary of the parsed device data generated ecmc hardware support snippets This is a utility/developer workflow, not a normal IOC startup script. Current Status The parser is currently described in utils/readme.md. The note in that file still applies: support is limited and mainly intended for slaves with several alternative PDO mappings.

item.title: EtherCAT Endpoint Timing
item.description: Purpose ecmc describes when an input value was acquired and when an output will be applied. The same model is used for encoders, digital inputs, drives and digital outputs, with or without Distributed Clocks (DC). It is the timing base for control-delay compensation, touch probes and position-triggered outputs. Generic timing model TIME ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────► input event application anchor A[k] output event E_in ●───────────────────────────────●────────────────────────────────● E_out │ │ │ └── input age Δin (< 0) ────────┘──── output lead Δout (> 0) ────┘ sample → copy → PDO → Rx control calculation → Tx → apply endpoint delay = E_out - E_in = Δout - Δin input terminal generation selection: sample ── calculation/copy time ── ready ─────────────────────────────► │ PDO frame after ready ──────────────┘ uses this sample PDO frame before ready ─────────────── uses the previous sample calculationCopyTimeNs determines which PDO generation is visible.

item.title: FSoE and TwinSAFE
item.description: Scope ecmccfg can map and cyclically forward Fail Safe over EtherCAT (FSoE) telegrams between TwinSAFE devices. The safety application itself must be configured and downloaded with TwinCAT or TwinSAFE Loader. ecmc and its operator panels are not safety-rated. They only transport and display process data. CRC, watchdog, connection validation, and the safety function remain in the certified FSoE/TwinSAFE devices. Direct cyclic forwarding The generic configuration uses Cfg.EcAddEntryCyclicWrite(<to>,<from>) instead of an ecmc PLC expression.

item.title: Slave firmware and identity
item.description: addSlave.cmd loads static identity records next to the existing HWType PV. slaveIdentity.cmd reads the values once after the hardware script, before runtime and iocInit, and passes them as initial values when loading the records. Slave PV suffix Value HWType Configured hardware description, such as EL2794 HWFw Firmware string read from CoE SDO 0x100A:00 HWRev Discovered SII revision, formatted as eight hexadecimal digits HWSer Discovered SII serial number, formatted as an unsigned decimal string HWFwStat Result of the optional firmware read HWIdStat Result of the revision/serial read Use the same slave prefix as HWType.

item.title: Verify DC Timing with Position Compare
item.description: Purpose This example verifies a timestamp-scheduled output against a hardware touch-probe latch. It is useful when checking whether Distributed Clock (DC) timing, terminal phase, wiring and ecmc position-compare prediction are good enough for position-triggered outputs. The tested setup is: ecmc axis position compare -> EL2252 timestamp-scheduled output pulse -> EL7062/ED7062 touch-probe input -> encoder touch-probe latched position + timestamp -> optional PLC reconstruction check The EL2252 proves the output timing. The EL7062/ED7062 touch probe proves when the electrical edge arrived and what encoder position the terminal latched at that edge.

item.title: Simulation backend (SIM=1)
item.description: SIM=1 selects ECMC’s memory-backed I/O driver for the selected master ID. Slave and entry declarations create typed memory instead of configuring a physical EtherCAT master. Motion, PLCs, limits, interlocks and master/slave coordination continue running in the IOC’s normal realtime cycle. The memory driver is not a device model. It does not automatically turn drive commands into enabled feedback or encoder movement. A separate Python model, PLC, manual PV client or other model must supply those inputs.
